main.summary: A United States-led coalition invaded Iraq in March 2003, opening a war that lasted until the withdrawal of American forces in 2011.

cards.heading: Iraq War
cards.text: A United States-led coalition invaded Iraq in March 2003, opening a war that lasted until the withdrawal of American forces in 2011. Bombing began on 20 March, with Britain, Australia and Poland joining the operation. The invasion overthrew Saddam Hussein's Ba'athist government. During the occupation, insurgents fought coalition forces and the newly established Iraqi government, extending the conflict beyond the initial campaign. President George W. Bush had received congressional authority to use force in October 2002 as part of his administration's wider war-on-terror policy. Iraq remained affected by armed conflict after the withdrawal.

main.title: Roman Polanski wins his first Oscar
main.subtitle: The directing award recognises The Pianist
main.summary: Roman Polanski received his first Oscar on 23 March 2003, winning the directing award for The Pianist. The film follows Władysław Szpilman, a Polish Jewish musician surviving the destruction of Warsaw during the Holocaust. Polanski was absent from the ceremony, and presenter Harrison Ford accepted the award on his behalf.

cards.heading: A directing Oscar for The Pianist
cards.text: Roman Polanski received his first Oscar on 23 March 2003, winning the directing award for The Pianist. The film follows Władysław Szpilman, a Polish Jewish musician surviving the destruction of Warsaw during the Holocaust. Polanski was absent from the ceremony, and presenter Harrison Ford accepted the award on his behalf.

cards.heading: A life reduced to places of shelter
cards.text: Adrien Brody plays Szpilman as the circumstances around him steadily narrow: professional life gives way to confinement, separation and concealment in a ruined city. Ronald Harwood adapted the pianist's memoir, keeping the story close to a survivor dependent on particular encounters and temporary places of safety. The film gives waiting and the management of ordinary needs a central place. Its movement through different shelters makes the destruction of the city tangible in the spaces where Szpilman tries to remain alive.

cards.heading: Recognition for an adaptation
cards.text: The Pianist had already received the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2002. At the 75th Oscars, Brody won leading actor and Harwood won adapted screenplay alongside Polanski's directing award. These distinct honours recognised the performance, writing and direction behind the same adaptation. Music is embedded in the subject's identity: the capacity to play survives through periods when public performance has become impossible, giving the eventual return to a keyboard a significance that extends beyond a concert scene.

main.title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
main.subtitle: Harry faces a school shaped by official denial
main.summary: The Order of the Phoenix begins with a wizarding government unwilling to accept Voldemort's return. Harry's account is challenged, and the Ministry's influence reaches Hogwarts through Dolores Umbridge. Her restrictions make the school a place where students have to negotiate what they are permitted to learn and say. Outside it, the Order gathers people prepared to oppose Voldemort. The fifth novel was published on 21 June 2003, following a release announcement issued jointly by Bloomsbury and Scholastic.

cards.heading: A warning nobody wants to hear
cards.text: The Order of the Phoenix begins with a wizarding government unwilling to accept Voldemort's return. Harry's account is challenged, and the Ministry's influence reaches Hogwarts through Dolores Umbridge. Her restrictions make the school a place where students have to negotiate what they are permitted to learn and say. Outside it, the Order gathers people prepared to oppose Voldemort. The fifth novel was published on 21 June 2003, following a release announcement issued jointly by Bloomsbury and Scholastic.

cards.heading: Lessons after class
cards.text: Harry and his friends respond to inadequate defence lessons by organizing their own practical training. The group gives classmates a reason to trust one another and a place to practise skills that official teaching withholds. Harry's anger and isolation complicate his role within it, while his connection to Voldemort makes even his own perceptions difficult to judge. Rowling links the public dispute over what is happening to the private strain of living through it, with exams, friendships and authority all pressing on the same increasingly frustrated teenager.

main.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
main.subtitle: The journey to Mount Doom reaches its conclusion
main.summary: The Return of the King had its world premiere in Wellington on 1 December 2003. Peter Jackson's third Tolkien film brought the journeys of the divided Fellowship towards their conclusion. Frodo and Sam approach Mount Doom under Gollum's guidance, while Gandalf helps defend Minas Tirith and Aragorn takes up his place among the leaders opposing Sauron. The film repeatedly moves between armies gathering for battle and two exhausted travellers whose task still depends on reaching the mountain.

cards.heading: The last road to Mordor
cards.text: The Return of the King had its world premiere in Wellington on 1 December 2003. Peter Jackson's third Tolkien film brought the journeys of the divided Fellowship towards their conclusion. Frodo and Sam approach Mount Doom under Gollum's guidance, while Gandalf helps defend Minas Tirith and Aragorn takes up his place among the leaders opposing Sauron. The film repeatedly moves between armies gathering for battle and two exhausted travellers whose task still depends on reaching the mountain.

cards.heading: The battle and the burden
cards.text: The defence of Minas Tirith expands the scale established at Helm's Deep: a city built in rising tiers faces siege engines, flying creatures and the armies on the Pelennor Fields. Against that spectacle, Frodo's strength and judgement continue to fail. Sam's persistence keeps the journey moving, giving the final approach a more personal urgency than the battles around it. The confrontation at the Black Gate then turns the military campaign into a diversion intended to help them finish their task.

cards.heading: A farewell to Middle-earth
cards.text: The film leaves time after the fighting for the return home and the departures that follow. The hobbits reach the Shire with experiences their neighbours have barely noticed, and Frodo's wounds remain part of the ending. Howard Shore's music connects these farewells to themes established across the trilogy. At the 2004 Academy Awards, The Return of the King won eleven Oscars, including Best Picture, Directing, Original Score and Original Song, completing the three-film production's run of annual releases.

main.title: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
main.summary: An undersea earthquake struck off Aceh in northern Sumatra on 26 December 2004.

cards.heading: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
cards.text: An undersea earthquake struck off Aceh in northern Sumatra on 26 December 2004. A rupture between tectonic plates produced a magnitude 9.2–9.3 earthquake and a tsunami that crossed the Indian Ocean. Waves reached up to thirty metres in some places, destroying coastal communities across fourteen countries. An estimated 227,898 people died, with Indonesia, Sri Lanka, India and Thailand among the worst affected. Survivors faced disrupted housing, services and livelihoods across extensive coastal areas. The scale of the disaster made it the deadliest recorded tsunami and one of the century's gravest natural catastrophes.

main.title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
main.subtitle: Alfonso Cuarón gives Harry's third year a colder atmosphere
main.summary: Sirius Black has escaped from prison, and Harry is told that the fugitive may be coming for him. Hogwarts is guarded by Dementors, whose presence draws him towards his parents' deaths rather than making him feel safe. Alfonso Cuarón takes over as director, working with cinematographer Michael Seresin and screenwriter Steve Kloves. Gary Oldman plays Black, David Thewlis joins as Professor Lupin and Michael Gambon becomes Dumbledore. The third film opened commercially in Britain and Ireland on 31 May 2004, followed by the United States on 4 June.

cards.heading: A different kind of threat
cards.text: Sirius Black has escaped from prison, and Harry is told that the fugitive may be coming for him. Hogwarts is guarded by Dementors, whose presence draws him towards his parents' deaths rather than making him feel safe. Alfonso Cuarón takes over as director, working with cinematographer Michael Seresin and screenwriter Steve Kloves. cards.heading: Returning to the same moment
cards.text: The film makes time and perspective part of the action. Incidents first seen without their full context return later with new information, allowing sounds and movements to acquire another meaning. That structure gives Harry and Hermione an active part in reinterpreting events the audience has already watched. Around it, the school feels more exposed to weather and the surrounding landscape, while the Dementors interrupt familiar journeys and games. John Williams's score supplies a quieter counterweight through A Window to the Past, connecting Harry's present fears with the family history he is trying to understand.

main.title: Hurricane Katrina
main.summary: Hurricane Katrina struck the southeastern United States in late August 2005, causing particularly severe destruction around New Orleans.

cards.heading: Hurricane Katrina
cards.text: Hurricane Katrina struck the southeastern United States in late August 2005, causing particularly severe destruction around New Orleans. The storm formed near the Bahamas on 23 August, crossed southeast Florida and intensified rapidly over the Gulf of Mexico. Its effects killed 1,392 people and caused an estimated 125 billion dollars in damage. The human toll made it the deadliest American hurricane since 1928, while the financial losses placed it among the country's costliest disasters. The name Katrina became closely associated with the extensive damage suffered by the city and surrounding region.

main.title: YouTube
main.summary: Chad Hurley, Jawed Karim and Steve Chen founded YouTube in February 2005 as an online video-sharing platform.

cards.heading: YouTube
cards.text: Chad Hurley, Jawed Karim and Steve Chen founded YouTube in February 2005 as an online video-sharing platform. It gave users a place to upload material and watch videos through the same service. Google purchased the company in November 2006 for 1.65 billion dollars. Advertising, creator revenue sharing and later paid subscriptions supported its expansion. Its audience and volume of uploads grew to an enormous scale, making video publishing an everyday activity for individuals as well as organisations. YouTube became a major route through which music, entertainment and other recorded material reached audiences.

main.title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
main.subtitle: An annotated textbook and lessons in Voldemort's history
main.summary: A second-hand Potions textbook helps Harry achieve unexpected success in class. Its handwritten improvements are useful, but its former owner's identity and intentions remain uncertain. At the same time, Harry suspects Draco Malfoy is working on something dangerous inside Hogwarts. J.K. Rowling's sixth novel appeared on 16 July 2005, with an Edinburgh Castle launch carried to audiences around the world. The story combines these questions with the changing friendships and romantic attachments of Harry's sixth year.

cards.heading: Notes in the margin

At the same time, Harry suspects Draco Malfoy is working on something dangerous inside Hogwarts. J.K. Rowling's sixth novel appeared on 16 July 2005, with an Edinburgh Castle launch carried to audiences around the world. The story combines these questions with the changing friendships and romantic attachments of Harry's sixth year.

cards.heading: A history that matters
cards.text: Dumbledore's private lessons send Harry into recorded memories of Voldemort's earlier life. Each visit supplies another piece of a history whose objects, ambitions and decisions now have practical importance. The investigation gives old conversations and apparently small possessions a place in the coming conflict. Harry is also learning to weigh the authority of teachers and the attractions of borrowed knowledge: the textbook can solve a classroom problem immediately, while understanding the past demands patience and judgement. Both strands turn on how much he knows about the person guiding him.

main.title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
main.subtitle: Mike Newell brings a dangerous tournament to Hogwarts
main.summary: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire puts an international competition at the centre of Harry's fourth school year. The enchanted cup names him as an additional champion even though he is too young to enter, leaving him to prepare for tasks involving a dragon, an underwater search and a maze. Mike Newell directs, with Robert Pattinson as Cedric Diggory and Brendan Gleeson as the new Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher, Alastor Moody. Released on 18 November 2005, the film makes Harry's growing public profile both an advantage and a source of danger.

cards.heading: An evening away from the contest
cards.text: The Yule Ball gives the competition another kind of pressure: the champions must dance before the other students, and finding a partner proves difficult in ways that have little to do with magic. Movement director Wayne McGregor choreographed the ball and the visiting schools' entrances, giving each group a distinct physical presence. Patrick Doyle replaced John Williams as composer. His Harry in Winter expands a brief moment from the film into a standalone orchestral piece, providing a quieter musical identity for Harry alongside the ceremonies and threats of the tournament.
